title: Late Breaking Results: Evaluation of Human Action Quality with Linear Recurrent Units and Graph Attention Networks on Embedded Systems
problem: Existing deep learning approaches for human pose estimation face significant memory consumption challenges on embedded systems. There is a gap in applying efficient state space models like Linear Recurrent Units to human action quality evaluation combined with spatial graph processing.
motivation: Linear recurrent units and state space models offer memory-efficient alternatives to transformers for capturing long-range temporal dependencies in human motion, enabling deployment on resource-constrained embedded systems.
method: The architecture combines Linear Recurrent Units (a type of state space model) with Graph Attention Networks to jointly model temporal and spatial aspects of human pose sequences. LRU captures long-range temporal dependencies across thousands of timesteps with linear memory complexity, while GAT processes the skeleton graph structure to model spatial relationships between joints. This hybrid approach enables efficient human action quality evaluation on embedded devices.
key_novelty: First application of linear recurrent units combined with graph attention networks for human action quality evaluation on embedded systems.
contributions: First application of state space models (S4, S4D, LRU) to human pose estimation and action quality evaluation
Novel hybrid SSM-GAT architecture for joint temporal and spatial modeling of human motion on embedded systems
Demonstration that state space models provide memory-efficient alternative to transformers for pose-based action understanding
Framework for deploying long-range sequence modeling on resource-constrained embedded hardware
limitations: The abstract does not provide specific quantitative metrics, speedup comparisons, energy consumption measurements, or detailed performance evaluation against baselines.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient human action quality assessment using state space models and graph attention networks for embedded deployment
